title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is section 10 of the continuation of La Longue Marche (manuscript p. 792). Grothendieck has a group, or a group-like object, M_{ρ,σ} presented in (195) as a fibre product N_ρ ×_γ N_σ ×_γ G_{ρ,σ}. Its elements are triples (a,b,u) whose images under the maps γ agree. The general Longue Marche setting is Galois–Teichmüller theory: profinite or discrete fundamental groups of moduli spaces and their 'arithmetic' subgroups. I cannot pin down from this page alone what ρ, σ and the groups denote. On this page he catalogues distinguished subobjects of M_{ρ,σ} and describes them through a semi-direct product decomposition M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ ≅ D*_12 ⋉ (G_a × S^+). Here μ_ρ is a central finite subgroup (roots of unity, or a centre). D*_12 is a group of order 12 acting by automorphisms; from the notation, plausibly a binary dihedral or 'dicyclic' group. G_a is a rank-one additive factor. S^+ is a further normal factor, with an intermediate subgroup M between G_a and G_a × S^+, giving M^♮_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ ≅ D*_12 ⋉ (G_a × M).

Steps on the page:
(200) The subgroup M(0), defined on the previous page as the triples with u in the fixer Z(0), contains μ_ρ. Modulo μ_ρ it is D*_12 ⋉ G_a, embedded in D*_12 ⋉ (G_a × S^+) via the canonical inclusion G_a ↪ G_a × S^+.
(201) Similarly M[0]/μ_ρ ≅ D*_12 ⋉ (G_a × L_0^M), where L_0^M is a subgroup of M, sitting inside M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ.
(202) A new subgroup M(1/2) = {(a,b,u) : u = b}. It lies in M^♮.
(203) Three facts:
- M(1/2) maps isomorphically onto the quotient Γ_{ρ,σ}.
- M^♮ = M(1/2)·M and M_{ρ,σ} = M(1/2)·S^+, i.e. M(1/2) is a complement (section) for the normal subgroups M and S^+.
(204) In the semi-direct product picture, M(1/2)/μ_ρ is the 'twisted diagonal' D*_12 ⋉ {(λ, λ(λ_1+λ_2)) : λ ∈ G_a}. It is the image of D*_12 ⋉ G_a under the D*_12-equivariant homomorphism G_a → G_a × M, λ ↦ (λ, λ(λ_1+λ_2)), where λ_1 + λ_2 is a fixed element of M.

The next page introduces M(-j) = {u = a}, which is again a complement but meets μ_ρ trivially. So there are several sections of M/μ_ρ → Γ/μ_ρ, indexed by 'weights' 0, 1/2, -j. This suggests a weight or filtration bookkeeping of sections, reminiscent of the choice of base points or tangential directions in Teichmüller-type groupoids.

Purpose: to classify canonical subgroups and sections (splittings) of an extension relevant to the Teichmüller tower in low dimension. This is presumably the dicyclic / SL_2(Z)-type symmetries of order 12 attached to M_{1,1} or M_{0,4}.
errors: No clear mathematical errors are visible. The identities are bookkeeping consequences of the fibre-product description (195).

Gap: the claim M(1/2)/μ_ρ ≅ D*_12·G_a requires the map λ ↦ (λ, λ(λ_1+λ_2)) to be D*_12-equivariant, i.e. λ_1+λ_2 must be D*_12-invariant in the appropriate twisted sense. This is not verified on the page.

ideas.what: Description of distinguished subgroups M(0), M[0], M(1/2) of a fibre-product group as semi-direct products D*_12 ⋉ (subgroups of G_a × S^+) modulo a central μ_ρ
ideas.modern_name: Complements/sections of a split extension; twisted diagonal subgroups in a semidirect product
ideas.where_published: Unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche (cote 140-4)

ideas.what: Family of distinct sections of M_{ρ,σ} → Γ_{ρ,σ} labelled by 'weights' 0, 1/2, -j, with differing intersections with μ_ρ
ideas.modern_name: Choice of splittings / base points (tangential base points) in Teichmüller-type groupoids; possibly related to weight-type labelling
ideas.usually_credited_to: unclear; tangential base points are due to Deligne (1989); Teichmüller groupoid splittings appear in work of Ihara, Nakamura and Schneps
ideas.where_published: Possibly connected to Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, groups of order 4 and 6 / 12)

missed.claim: A systematic list of sections of M_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ over Γ_{ρ,σ}/μ_ρ with 'weights' 0, 1/2, -j, embedded in a D*_12-equivariant semidirect product framework. This is part of an unpublished detailed treatment of low-dimensional Teichmüller-type groups. It is technical, and its meaning cannot be fixed without the surrounding definitions.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It may document Grothendieck's own handling of the order-12 symmetries and the choice of base sections in the genus-0/1 Teichmüller groupoid. This is of mainly historical interest unless the definitions on earlier pages reveal a non-standard structure.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine structural bookkeeping: subgroups, complements and twisted diagonals in a semidirect product. It sits within an unpublished but technical development, and nothing stands out as a new result.
transcription_corrections: Top margin reads roughly 'NB [crossed out] μ_ρ ⊂ M_{ρ,σ}(0) ⊂ M_{ρ,σ}[0] i.e.'.
In (202) the condition is written with a capital 'U = b'.
The superscript on M_{ρ,σ} in (202)–(204) is a special arrow-like symbol (like ≨ or ⇂), not clearly ♮.
In (203) the target Γ_{ρ,σ} is underlined.
In (201) the factor is 'L_0^{M}' with M underlined over L_0.
The margin note at (204) reads 'μ_ρ ⊂ M_{ρ,σ}(1/2)'.
The factor read as G_a could be G_m or 'G_o' in the hand; the previous page's transcription uses ΓG_m.
